topic: Sound Waves and the Doppler Effect
key_concepts: Longitudinal waves move particles parallel to the direction of wave travel
Compressions are regions where particles are closer together with higher pressure and dens
Rarefactions are regions where particles are farther apart with lower pressure and density
Sound is produced by vibrations or oscillations in a medium
Sound requires a source of vibration, a medium, and a receiver
Sound travels as longitudinal or compression waves
Sound travels faster in solids than in liquids and gases because particles are closer toge
Pitch is the highness or lowness of sound and depends on frequency
Loudness depends on amplitude, with greater amplitude producing louder sound
Increasing tension in a string raises the pitch of the sound
The Doppler effect causes higher pitch when a sound source approaches and lower pitch when
Sound cannot travel without a medium
